details: CONFIRMED by reading: the example and the standard-terms bullet contradict each other in the same rule file, which the owner's
sessions load (and which reaches it-terms-ru, it-terms-es, design-track and explain-existing through append_system_prompt).
Whether a session actually writes "изменения" for commits is PLAUSIBLE (no grader checks commit). Owner decision broken: English
IT terms stay in English (memory: use-english-it-terms; the bullet itself). Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: "- Standard IT terms stay in their English form ...: merge, branch, commit, fast-forward, hook, ..."
"... case it needs ("несколько изменений", "после merge"), or leave the term uninflected."
-"... сдвинуться вперёд на эти commit'ы" (the owner read this reply and approved it).
failing_case: rules/working-with-me.md:58-62 says: "Turn the Russian words around the term into the case it needs ("несколько изменений",
"после merge")". "несколько изменений" holds no English term at all: it shows commit replaced by "изменения". The bullet
just above (line 47-48) lists commit among the standard terms that stay in English and says the local word "does not appear
in your reply at all". The no-calques grader's PASS example was changed the same way ("сдвинуться вперёд на эти изменения",
where it had commit'ы). A session that follows the example writes "несколько изменений" where the owner expects commit; the
english-terms-kept grader checks only merge, branch, fast-forward and hook, so the eval does not see it.
Now: the example teaches dropping the term. Should: the example keeps the term and inflects only the words around it.
fix_hint: Replace "несколько изменений" with an example that keeps the term ("в нескольких commit", "после трёх commit"); give the
no-calques PASS example an uninflected term too ("на эти commit"); update the asserted string in tests/test_claudemd_fixes.py;
pass_cases: 1. The rule bullet's examples each contain the English term: e.g. "в нескольких commit" or "после трёх commit", "после merge".
2. The bullet still says no apostrophe before a Russian ending and still names "commit'ов" as the wrong form (test_ru_style
test_q1_the_rule_holds_the_three_lines keeps passing).
3. The no-calques grader's PASS example keeps an English term where it had commit'ы (or drops that clause), and
tests/test_claudemd_fixes.py asserts the new string.
4. python3 evals/plugin/system_rules.py rewrites the four prompt.md lines; tests/test_eval_system_rules.py passes.
findings.summary: the new rule's example "несколько изменений" replaces commit with a Russian word, against the bullet above it that keeps commit in English

details: PLAUSIBLE: the judge may well work (the rubric quotes the exact bad forms), but nothing measures it, and the only test of it
passes with the behaviour removed. evals/judge-measure/README.md: that folder "measures that judge on recorded replies before
it gates anything"; graders.test.sh already supports recorded/bad/<llm grader>__*.txt listed in judge-measure items. The
other it-terms-ru llm graders are not measured either, so this follows existing practice, but the brief's "Done when" asks for
proof of Q1 and the gender/opener half of Q1 has none. Size: 30 minutes plus one small paid judge run (a few items, well under $1).
evidence: tests/test_ru_style.py:40-44: assertIn("type: llm"), assertIn("masculine"), assertIn("not named") on the grader text.
failing_case: tests/test_ru_style.py test_q1_the_case_judges_gender_and_opener asserts only that the file contains "type: llm", "masculine"
and "not named". Replace the rubric body with "PASS always." plus those three words in a comment and the test still passes.
The paid run showed the judge PASS three good replies; no run shows it FAIL the live bad ones the queue item cites
("в отдельной branch" beside "в отдельном branch"; the opener "Речь о вашем проекте: название и назначение в сообщении не
прозвучали, поэтому я их не называю."). The queue item promises the case checks gender and opener "by its judge"; that check
is unproven, unlike the regex grader, which graders.test.sh runs against a recorded bad reply.
Now: a judge that passes everything goes unnoticed. Should: the two live bad replies are recorded and judged FAIL.

details: CONFIRMED with Python re (same semantics as the bun RegExp here). Models rarely emit U+2018 in that place, so it is fragile,
not wrong in the measured runs. Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: python3 probe: 'несколько commit‘ов' True ; 'несколько commit`ов' True ; "после PR'а" False (True = passes the grader).
failing_case: Python re with the grader's pattern: "несколько commit‘ов" (U+2018 LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK) -> pattern matches (PASS);
"несколько commit`ов" -> PASS. Both should FAIL like "commit'ов" and "commit’ов" do.
fix_hint: Widen the class to [’'ʼ‘`] and add the two inputs to test_q1_the_apostrophe_grader...
pass_cases: 1. "несколько commit‘ов" fails the grader.
2. "несколько commit`ов" fails the grader.
3. "Это несколько commit'ов." and "Это несколько commit’ов." still fail (test_ru_style line 27-28).
4. "Это merge, а don't значит не надо." and recorded/good/merge-reply.txt still pass.
findings.summary: the apostrophe class misses U+2018 and the backtick, so "commit‘ов" passes the grader
